answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it can post offers or vote. A peer who accepts an offer risks part of its own stake, and verified disputes slash the dishonest party’s lock; repeated behavior builds a history that cannot be transferred to fresh accounts. The saffron trader by the willow inlet can still join, but an attacker seeking influence must buy and immobilize real capital for every sybil, then risk losing it.
